rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 - Just Cause for Termination
rules.requirement: Landlords may not terminate a residential tenancy without just cause after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied the property for 12 months (or 24 months if an adult tenant is added before 24 months). Just cause is categorized into at-fault and no-fault reasons, and no-fault evictions require relocation assistance or a final month rent waiver equal to one month's rent.
rules.key_value: 1 month rent relocation assistance for no-fault evictions

coverage.summary: Applies to residential real property after 12 or 24 months of continuous occupancy, excluding hotels, institutional housing, certain owner-occupied properties, housing less than 15 years old, separately alienable properties under specific non-corporate ownership, and deed-restricted affordable housing.
coverage.owner_condition: Exempts certain single-family owner-occupied residences, owner-occupied duplexes, and non-corporate separately alienable properties meeting statutory ownership and notice requirements.
coverage.unresolvable: Tenancy duration and specific ownership corporate structures require facts beyond a simple address record.

rules.exemptions: Transient occupancy, nonprofit/religious/extended care/residential care facilities, dormitories, shared bathroom/kitchen with owner, certain single-family owner-occupied residences (including ADUs/JADUs or mobilehomes), owner-occupied two-unit structures, housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, certain separately alienable properties (not owned by a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member) with proper notice, and deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing.
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
